name: Habitat for Humanity
quote: Severe storms in the Pacific are only getting worse, but through your donations we can reduce their impact.
description:
New Zealand

Habitat for Humanity holds the fundamental belief that everyone deserves a decent place to live. Habitat for Humanity’s housing initiatives and advocacy efforts in Aotearoa New Zealand and the Pacific are all designed to build pathways that lead towards an adequate home, whatever that may mean for a person or family’s personal journey, culture or circumstance. From supplying curtains to facilitating home ownership, Habitat’s many pathways are formed on the pillars of education, adequacy and stability through safe shelter.

The Problem

The Pacific Islands face ever-increasing severe weather that affects homes and livelihoods, including an annual cyclone season. Often homes are damaged or destroyed by high tides, storms, or natural disasters while still recovering from the last severe event. Repairs and strengthening of homes can be limited by access to finances, specific skills, or materials in remote locations.

The Solution

Habitat for Humanity partners with communities in Samoa, Fiji and Tonga through community trainings. Shelter trainings are run by local organisations for local communities to make themselves and their homes more resilient. When the next weather event occurs, communities are better prepared with strengthened housing and the skills to recover quickly if needed.
Local communities develop plumbing skills, home repair knowledge, and community action plans to make their homes better prepared for extreme weather and a changing environment.
